What is kitchen art wall decor?

Kitchen art wall decor refers to prints, paintings, or illustrated artworks chosen specifically to hang in a kitchen or kitchen-diner space, adding personality, colour, and warmth to what is often a purely functional room. It can range from botanical prints and food-inspired illustrations to typographic quotes and abstract designs — anything that makes the kitchen feel more like a curated, lived-in home. In recent years, French Country and botanical styles have become especially popular choices, thanks to their timeless, relaxed quality that suits both traditional and contemporary kitchens. A well-chosen set of kitchen art wall decor can completely change the feel of the room, making it a more welcoming place to cook, eat, and gather. Sets of three prints are a particularly popular format because they create an instant, balanced gallery-wall look without the guesswork of curating individual pieces.

How to Hang Kitchen Art Wall Decor: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide

1. Choose your wall and measure the space: Find a clear stretch of wall — above a dining table, beside the cooker, or along a run of cabinets works well. Measure the width so you know how much room you have for all three prints side by side.

2. Decide on the layout before you hang: Lay all three prints out on the floor first and adjust the spacing until it looks right — usually 5 to 8 cm between each print is a good starting point. Take a photo so you can refer to it when you're up the ladder.

3. Find the right height: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level — around 145 to 155 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If you're hanging them above a piece of furniture, aim for 15 to 20 cm above the top of the furniture.

4. Mark and hang: Use a pencil to lightly mark where each hook or nail will go, double-check with a spirit level, and then hang the prints. Step back and adjust any that need a small nudge.

5. Style around them: Once they're up, bring in complementary textures — linen, wood, wicker, or a small potted herb — to tie the botanical, French Country feel together.

Available in Luster art paper (slight sheen, vibrant tones) or Museum quality paper (smooth, matte, gallery-style finish).

Framed Print — The print comes already mounted and framed, ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and ideal if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper finishes.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and wrapped tightly around a wooden stretcher frame, giving a contemporary, borderless look. Arrives ready to hang. No glass, no frame — just clean, textured botanical art on the wall. Available in a range of canvas size options.

How to Style Pink Pictures in Your Office or Home

I'd hang all three of these prints in a straight horizontal row at eye level, with even gaps between each one — it gives the set a neat, gallery-style look that works brilliantly in a home office or study. The soft pink, blue, and white palette means they sit beautifully against white, pale grey, or even a soft sage-green wall. If you want a really pulled-together feel, pick up one of those tones in a desk accessory, a cushion, or a small plant pot nearby. The country cottage mood these prints carry also makes them a natural fit for a kitchen, hallway, or bedroom — anywhere you want a little warmth and personality.

Choosing the Right Size and Finish for Your Walls

When it comes to picking the right size for this set, think about the wall space you have to work with. A narrower wall — like the space between two windows or above a small desk — suits the smaller sizes beautifully, keeping things light and uncluttered. If you have a longer stretch of wall, go bigger: the flower shop detail really rewards the extra space, and the loose watercolour linework looks especially lovely at a larger scale. As a general rule, the combined width of all three prints (including any gaps between them) should take up roughly two-thirds of the wall width — this keeps things balanced and intentional.

What are pink pictures?

Pink pictures are wall art prints that feature pink as a dominant or accent colour, used to add warmth, softness, and personality to a room. They range from bold abstract pieces to delicate florals and charming illustrative scenes, making them one of the most versatile choices in home decor. Pink tones work across many interior styles — from country cottage and vintage to modern and Scandi — and pair naturally with whites, blues, greens, and neutrals. A set of pink pictures, like this watercolour flower shop trio, can tie a room together and give it a cohesive, welcoming feel without overwhelming the space.

How to Hang Pink Pictures as a Set of 3 in Your Office

1. Plan your layout first: Lay all three prints out on the floor or a table before you touch the walls. Decide whether you want a straight horizontal row (clean and classic) or a slight offset (more relaxed and gallery-like). For this flower shop set, a horizontal row at eye level works best.

2. Mark your centre point: Find the centre of the wall space you are working with and mark it lightly with a pencil. Hang the middle print first, centred on that mark, then work outwards to the left and right prints with an even gap between each — around 5 to 8 cm looks neat without feeling cramped.

3. Use a spirit level: Even a small tilt is very noticeable across a row of three. A small spirit level (or a spirit-level app on your phone) takes seconds to use and makes a real difference to the finished result.

4. Step back and check: Before you commit to all the hooks, hold or prop each print in position and step back across the room. Check the height feels right — prints generally look best when the centre of the group sits at eye level, roughly 145–150 cm from the floor.

5. Consider the surroundings: Once hung, look at what is already in the room. Add a small pink or blue accent nearby — a plant pot, a pen holder, a notebook — to echo the colours in the prints and tie the whole look together.

Luster Paper — A semi-gloss finish that gives colours a gentle brightness and sheen. A great all-round choice that suits the fresh pinks and blues in this set beautifully.
